Let the eigenvalues of \(PH_t\) be positive. For any fixed \(P\), write
\[
m=\min_{t\in[0,1]}\lambda_{\min}(PH_t),\qquad
M=\max_{t\in[0,1]}\lambda_{\max}(PH_t).
\]
Then the best step size is
\[
\eta=\frac{2}{M+m},
\]
and the resulting worst spectral radius is
\[
\frac{M-m}{M+m}=\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1},\qquad \kappa=\frac{M}{m}.
\]

For the unrestricted case, the generalized eigenvalues of \((H_1,H_0)\) are the roots of
\[
\det(H_1-\lambda H_0)=\lambda^2-3\lambda+1,
\]
so
\[
\alpha=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2},\qquad \beta=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad \alpha\beta=1.
\]
For any \(P\), if both endpoint spectra lie in \([m,M]\), then the spectrum of \(H_0^{-1}H_1\) lies in \([m/M,M/m]\), forcing
\[
\kappa\ge \beta.
\]
This is attained by the geometric-mean preconditioner, which makes the spectra along the segment lie in
\[
[\beta^{-1/2},\beta^{1/2}],
\]
so \(\kappa_{\mathrm{full}}=\beta\). Hence
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{full}}
=\frac{\beta-1}{\beta+1}
=\frac1{\sqrt5}.
\]

For diagonal \(P\), scale \(P=\operatorname{diag}(1,y)\), \(z=\sqrt y\). The endpoint preconditioned symmetric forms are
\[
S_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&z\\ z&2z^2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
S_1=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&z\\ z&4z^2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both have determinant \(y\). After dividing by \(\sqrt y=z\), their traces are
\[
\tau_0=\frac1z+2z,\qquad \tau_1=\frac1{2z}+4z.
\]
The largest eigenvalue is increasing in the trace because the normalized determinant is \(1\). Thus we minimize
\[
\max(\tau_0,\tau_1).
\]
The optimum occurs when \(\tau_0=\tau_1\), giving
\[
\frac1z+2z=\frac1{2z}+4z
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad z=\frac12,
\]
and then \(\tau_0=\tau_1=3\). Therefore the normalized largest eigenvalue is
\[
\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}=\beta,
\]
so
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{diag}}=\beta^2.
\]
Thus
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}
=\frac{\beta^2-1}{\beta^2+1}
=\frac{\sqrt5}{3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\rho_{\mathrm{full}},\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}\right)
=
\left(\frac1{\sqrt5},\frac{\sqrt5}{3}\right)}
\]
